title: After the Flood
premise: An original museum story: a conservator has already dried and stabilized a flood-damaged map. Document it, protect it, and tell its story without erasing the damage. Not instructions for treating a real collection.

items.label: Archive letter
items.description: A fictional letter says its writer carried a map on this journey. It is a clue, not conclusive proof that this is that map.

items.label: Damaged map
items.description: The same dry, stabilized map will stay with us through housing and display. Its old water marks remain part of its history.

items.label: Documented map
items.description: The map with its condition record. Recording the damage has not repaired or replaced it.

items.label: Exhibition label
items.description: This flood-marked map may have travelled with the letter’s writer. The association remains uncertain.

items.label: Housed map
items.description: The supported map has a protective enclosure. It was dry and stabilized before housing.

items.label: Map exhibit
items.description: A map, its scars and an honestly qualified story. The label preserves uncertainty as well as provenance.

items.label: Map measurements
items.description: Dimensions recorded beside the supported map, without pressing a ruler onto its fragile surface.

items.label: Protected display
items.description: The same supported map is displayed under controlled low light; preservation does not make its past disappear.

items.label: Provenance note
items.description: The letter may connect this map with a journey. The note records that attribution and its uncertainty, not a proven chain of ownership.

items.label: Supported map
items.description: The same map rests on a suitable rigid support, reducing the need to handle the sheet itself.

recipes.description: The conservator records dimensions beside the supported sheet without pressing the ruler onto its surface.

stages.title: The salvage table
stages.speaker: The conservator
stages.motivation: Our conservator has dried and stabilized this map. Before we display it, make a record of its condition.

area.label: The salvage table
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

stages.title: The paper store
stages.speaker: The conservator
stages.motivation: We will not make the tears disappear. Give the map a protective housing.

area.label: The paper store
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: Conservation supplies
caches.narrative: The store provides suitable board, tissue, folders and a cutting tool. Treatment decisions belong to a trained conservator.

stages.title: The quiet gallery
stages.speaker: The curator
stages.motivation: A letter tells us who carried the map. Make a protected exhibit that keeps that history visible.

area.label: The quiet gallery
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: Archive and display store
caches.narrative: The archive supplies a related letter; the gallery provides a label and a low-light case.

sources.title: Canadian Conservation Institute: Care of paper objects
sources.note: Primary preventive conservation guidance; fiction abstracts safe housing, not wet-object treatment.

notes: Original scenario candidate. It tests preservation as progress rather than every output becoming a more powerful version.
No recipe adds water, heat, adhesive or cleaning chemicals to a damaged artifact.
Version2: item descriptions provide inspectable semantic content. Same recipe graph and checkpoints as v1; new text does not constitute human fun validation.
